entities.summary:
Charles I de Montmorency was a 14th-century French noble who played a pivotal role in the Hundred Years' War. He was the son of John II, Duke of Bourbon, and his wife, Catherine de Valois. Born around 1319, Charles I de Montmorency became a prominent military leader and strategist, known for his bravery and tactical genius. He fought alongside his father at the Battle of Crécy in 1346 and later became the leader of the Burgundian army during the Battle of Agincourt in 1415. Charles I de Montmorency's legacy extended beyond his military prowess, as he also played a key role in the development of the French nobility and the rise of the Burgundian dynasty. He died on September 11, 1381, at the age of 61, leaving behind a son, John II de Montmorency, who would go on to become a prominent figure in French politics.

Charles I de Montmorency was a key figure in the Hundred Years' War, which was fought between England and France from 1337 to 1453. He was one of the most prominent military leaders of the war, known for his bravery and tactical genius. His leadership played a crucial role in several key battles, including the Battle of Crécy and the Battle of Agincourt.

The legacy of Charles I de Montmorency can be seen in the development of the French nobility and the rise of the Burgundian dynasty. His son, John II de Montmorency, would go on to become a prominent figure in French politics and continue his father's legacy. Charles I de Montmorency's contributions to the Hundred Years' War and the French nobility have had a lasting impact on European history.

In conclusion, Charles I de Montmorency was a significant figure in 14th-century France, known for his military prowess and leadership during the Hundred Years' War. His legacy continues to be felt today, with his contributions to the development of the French nobility and the rise of the Burgundian dynasty remaining an important part of European history.
